summary: Added operator root loading and injectable connector factory; async confined traversal derives all six signals without following symlinks, uses no-follow regular-file handles, enforces scan entry/read/deadline caps, and warns on incomplete secret coverage.

evidence.observation: Before edits, an escaping file symlink read an external fake AWS key and a linked external SECURITY.md passed. Evidence contains no credential bytes.

evidence.coverage: Environment roots, production/OIDC/empty disabling, malformed config, lazy default environment, explicit root copying, nested roots, missing allowed roots, filesystem-root aliases, outside/sibling/traversal, repository/file/directory/workflow/policy/lockfile symlinks, directory loops, FIFOs/device links, open-time symlink replacement, six IDs/requirement mappings, secret redaction, per-file/total bytes, entries including directories/skips, deadline/abort cleanup.

evidence.observation: Actual developer root smoke: lockfile pass; secrets warn, findings [], complete false, reason individual file byte limit reached; 2084 entries and 7318814 bytes in observed snapshot.

limitations: Node provides no portable dirfd-relative openat API. O_NOFOLLOW protects the final file component; malicious concurrent ancestor directory replacements can race repeated canonical-path/inode checks. Allowed directory structures must be controlled by trusted operators.

Filesystem calls cannot be cancelled. The 15-second deadline stops further work after the in-flight operation resolves and all handles are closed; a hung filesystem may exceed this deadline. The enclosing registry must bound caller wait and retain its concurrency slot until underlying work settles.

The real project has tracked framework JSON and review artifacts above 512000 bytes. Its default developer scan truthfully reports secrets warn with no findings and incomplete individual-file coverage; root coordinator authorized adapting the API assertion rather than broad exclusions.
Focused tests use temporary roots only. Full integration/suite verification is owned by the coordinator; actual device nodes and hostile concurrent ancestor swaps are not reproduced.
